steps.title: Intent
in: The product concern, in their words: a new entry to create, or the change to an existing entry
out: Functional intent: the entry to create, or the entry to change and how

steps.title: Auditor
steps.actor: AI: a single auditor, who holds the discussion with the human
in: Vision, functional guidelines and vocabulary, plus the entries whose scope overlaps the intent's (the entry to change, when there is one). Selected by script, index first. Never the code
Need entries and parcours whose scope overlaps the intent's. Selected by script, index first
out: Delta: overlaps, contradicts, modifies, hole, existing flows touched. Three fields per line: entry, consequence, proposed resolution. Empty if nothing to report
Proposed scope, drawn from the project vocabulary. To validate at the gate

steps.title: Challenge
steps.actor: Human F, opened by script only if the delta is not empty
in: The delta, short and in fixed form
On request: a question to the auditor about a line of the delta
out: Revised intent, back to the audit
The auditor's answer, read-only, quoting the entry concerned. It modifies no document: only a revised intent has an effect

steps.title: Writer
out: Proposed entry in fixed format: vision, functional guideline or vocabulary, with its scope and what it replaces. New entry: a file created at `<domain>/<id>.md`. Existing entry: that same file, same id

steps.title: Validator
steps.actor: Persona distinct from the lead: it receives the deliverable alone, never the discussion

steps.title: Code checks
out: Valid schema, scope from the vocabulary, ambiguous words, vocabulary without duplicates, each statement cites its source, no scope overlap with an accepted entry without "replaces"

steps.title: Judge
steps.actor: AI, three fixed questions, citation required

questions.q: Is each sentence of the intent carried?
Is a statement unsupported by its cited source?
Is there a contradiction with a cited entry?

out: Yes or no: is each sentence of the intent carried? a statement unsupported by its cited source? a contradiction with a cited entry?

steps.title: Gate · Review
in: Code checks and judge, all green
out: Or changes: back to the intent

steps.title: Accepted · merge
out: Entry created or changed in the wiki, accepted, with its scope. The Prototype and Need read it

contract: A product concern: a principle to set, a recurring line, vocabulary to fix, a new scope to define, a repeated local rule (promotion), or a correction of an existing frame entry.
An accepted global wiki entry, new or changed: vision, functional guideline or vocabulary.
Human F, at the gate. No human T.
notes: A script opens it only if the auditor's delta is not empty. Otherwise writing follows directly. The discussion is a loop between the human and the auditor, with no maximum number of rounds: at each round, the auditor receives the delta and the messages exchanged since its last round.
The same workflow creates a new entry or changes an existing one (its id never changes). Removing an entry is not a run: a human decides it, and the script refuses while another entry cites it.
Unlike the technical frame, nothing is run in CI and nothing blocks. The Prototype and Need read these entries, and their auditor flags a gap in its delta. The human decides.
There is nothing to implement, so nothing to prove: no tests written first, no second gate.
Defining or modifying it is a decision of this workflow, with a gate: for example the product domains.
Performance, security and accessibility stay in the Technical frame, decided by human T alone.
The audit ignores the code. Discarded alternatives: nothing is kept for now.
They belong to the Persona and User flow workflows: they are different entries, serving the Recette.
doc.lede: The functional frame is what the product does in shared terms: its vision, its vocabulary and the rules several behaviors have in common. A human F creates or changes one of its entries, which becomes an accepted global wiki entry. These are landmarks that the Prototype and Need read for awareness, not blocking rules.
